title: The proposed theta series can diverge on its stated domain
reason: For j = 0, u = 1 and c(n) = exp(πn²), every summand equals 1. Even bounded coefficients c(n) = 1 give the same divergence at u = 0. The source defines a totalized sum and proves classical summability under boundedness and u > 0.
proposed_correction: State the classical definition on u > 0 under an explicit summability assumption, for example |c(n)| ≤ 1. To retain Lean’s full domain, explain that a nonsummable sum and the real square root at negative u are assigned zero.

title: The ordinary tail integrals can diverge for the allowed coefficients
reason: Take j=0, T=1 and c(p)=p² exp(πp²) on primes, zero otherwise, so μc=−c. Both theta series converge for every u>1. On 1<u<1+p⁻² the p term of θc(u)/u is at least p² exp(−3π)/√2, so the integral receives a fixed positive contribution from every prime. Thus J is infinite and the ordinary complex mollifier integral diverges at s=1/2. Lean uses totalized integrals and proves integrability under bounded coefficients.
proposed_correction: Impose |c(n)|≤1 before introducing the ordinary integrals, or state their summability/integrability domain and explain Lean’s values outside it.

title: The character of lift j has weight −κⱼ
reason: The table calls the positive integer κⱼ the character’s weight. The character used in the lift has archimedean exponent −κⱼ at every place, as the explicit HasWeight declaration and the lift-characters page both say.
proposed_correction: Keep κⱼ=κ+(j+½)Δ and label it the negative of the weight of the character of lift j.

title: Coupling divisibility needs a bound on the exponential scale
reason: The passage from divisibility of the substituted couplings to integral coefficients also uses |(ϖ^(p+1)/p)π|ₚ ≤ p^(−1/(p−1)). A normal form allows arbitrary ϖ. Without the bound, the factorial denominators of the exponential can survive. The substitution must consist of integral series with zero constant term.
proposed_correction: Include the norm condition and the two conditions on Z where the chapter states the integrality criterion. For the theta application one may instead specify the scale v(ϖ)=ρₚ and record that it supplies the norm bound.

title: Use the normalized sigma function that defines θ
reason: The link identifies σ with the classical Weierstrass sigma. The source defines the odd theta section with derivative 1 at zero and multiplier χ(ℓ)exp(H(ℓ,z)+H(ℓ,ℓ)/2). It explicitly records an exp(cz²) factor relative to classical sigma. Translating by t and dividing by the value at zero leaves the nonconstant factor exp(c(z²+2tz)), changing θ and g.
proposed_correction: Define σ through its normalized transformation law with H(ℓ,z)=πℓ̄z/area Λ and χ=+1 on 2Λ, −1 elsewhere. Link that definition where θ is introduced and distinguish its relationship to classical sigma.

title: The theta-product application omits the integrality hypothesis on H
reason: The cited normal-form theorem requires H to be an integral series in the coordinates y(u_j†z). The remark leaves H unrestricted. For the empty diagram the jet is F(0), and θ(0) = 1. Taking H = p^(−M) gives |F(0)| = p^M, exceeding the stated p^(f N³) bound for M > f N³.
proposed_correction: In the remark require H ∈ O[[y(u_j†z) : j ∈ J]], as in the normal-form theorem. Keep the main bound for F already known to have the normal form.

title: Both six-copy conclusions are upper bounds of zero
reason: The spanning statement at line 49 and the inert-frame statement at line 57 each assert an equality. Both prove val₆(ν) ≤ 0. For the first, take μ(z)=z/p and multiplicity zero. The integral multiple pμ spans the coordinate, but the permissible series y(z/p) has linear coefficient 1/p. The inert specialization also concludes only an upper bound in Cases.lean:220.
proposed_correction: Change the link texts at lines 49 and 57 to “least valuation at most zero” and carry the wording into both linked leaf titles.

title: The mirror and glued identities require a target translate and scalar
reason: An unmodified mirror lift is described as Up after a direct lift, and a glued double lift as two direct lifts after Up. In the first formula the target is acted on by D_N=diag(1,…,1,N⁻¹), as in line 714 of the source. In the second, the same target translate is required and the right-hand side is multiplied by the number of primitive vectors times γ′γ. Both identities apply to ramified input.
proposed_correction: Say that the D_N-translate of the mirror lift equals Up of the direct lift on ramified vectors, and that the D_N-translate of the raw glued pair equals the stated scalar times the two direct lifts after Up.

title: The bound requires automorphic characters
reason: The theorem allows characters of U(1)(A) with specified weights and tame parts, but the source requires continuous unitary characters trivial on rational norm-one points. The stated local data only control points integral at finite places. At a split place w, for example, u ↦ ξ^ord_w(u_w) for transcendental ξ of modulus one is trivial on integral points and has weight zero. A complex field automorphism can send ξ off the unit circle. The argument on line 44 cannot discard this factor for arbitrary finite determinants.
proposed_correction: Require a and b to be automorphic characters of U(1)(E⁺)\U(1)(A). For arbitrary finite determinants cite AutChar.HasWeight.norm_map_eq_one (Lib/ClassField/HeckeCharacter/AlgebraicValues.lean:369), which uses algebraic base change.

title: Require automorphic characters in the kernel theorem
reason: Characters of the adelic group with specified archimedean exponents and tame parts can be nontrivial on rational points. For example a unitary character of the valuation at one split finite place is trivial on integral units and can detect a rational element of norm one. Rational invariance in part 1 and its proof requires both twists to be trivial on the rational norm-one subgroup.
proposed_correction: Take a and b to be continuous circle-valued automorphic characters of the norm-one adeles, trivial on rational norm-one points, with the indicated weights and tame parts. Link this condition in the opening sentence.

title: The doubled grid parameter lists twice the half-integral centre parameter
reason: The linked centre-system definition uses λ_B in half-integer units. At z=1 and o=i=j=0, the node has no blocks or lowering: its doubled base entry is 2λ^Y_{τ,n}+1 (Parameters.lean:123), while λ_B has entry λ^Y_{τ,n}+½. The two vectors cannot be identified as asserted.
proposed_correction: Write l^o_{i,j}=2λ_B under the signed indexing (equivalently, l^o_{i,j}/2 lists λ_B), and preserve this convention in the proof.

title: The stated index range can place an undefined centre in B
reason: The page only introduces u_l,d_l for l<m and links a definition requiring B⊆C. The allowed choice o=j=0, i=m+1 puts u_m in B. Lean's parameter theorem genuinely allows this i because it defines the labels on ℕ ⊕ ℕ. Its separate containment lemma needs i≤m as well as o+j≤m.
proposed_correction: Define u_l,d_l for every natural l, distinguish the first m of each as C, and use the ambient-label definition of IsParam. If presenting only nodes inside the finite grid, say so and add i≤m to item 3 and appropriate bounds to the recurrences.

title: The stated signature count fails for j greater than m
reason: The entrywise sign rule is given for every natural j, but its asserted counts k+j−1 and m−j need j≤m. At j=m+1 the threshold is r+1, so all r entries are positive, whereas the text counts r+1 positive signs. The source proves the count for the lift indices 1≤j≤m in Rows.lean.
proposed_correction: Restrict the count to 0≤j≤m, including the convention for j=0, or give the all-j counts min(r,k+j−1) and r−min(r,k+j−1).

title: The string description stops one stage before the top
reason: The grading Y_j=X_j plus a string holds for j<m. At j=m the separate last grading has n_m−1 grade-zero coordinates and an empty string. Y_m lies inside X_m with codimension one, reversing the inclusion in the notation paragraph. An even-length string at earlier stages also has no middle vector of norm −N.
proposed_correction: Restrict the description to j<m and mention the middle norm only when the string length is odd. Give the separate codimension-one description of Y_m used for restriction.

title: The top stage has zero string vectors
reason: Part 4 permits k=m−1 but assigns the string length m−2−k, which is −1 at that endpoint with ordinary subtraction. The Lean expression is natural-number subtraction and equals zero there. The subsequent proof of the full lower chain invokes exactly this endpoint with the last grading.
proposed_correction: Use max(0,m−2−k), or give m−2−k for k≤m−2 and zero for k=m−1. Explicitly identify the empty-string case with the last grading.

title: The quotient modulo β can be infinite
reason: The scaling hypotheses only make β a unit above N. For a place v away from N, take β to be zero at v and one elsewhere, with δ=1 and all κ_i=1. This satisfies the hypotheses and the residue ring has a quotient O_v, which is infinite. The claimed finite target for Lagrange’s theorem and the ordinary finite count in part 2 do not follow. Lean uses Nat.card of the target, equal to zero when it is infinite.
proposed_correction: State the finite-or-zero counting convention for the matrix space. If the target is infinite the finite away-quotient order divides 0. For a finite target apply the kernel argument in the text. A positive numerical bound requires finite index of (β), as holds for the specific level used later.

title: The lattice bounds use the chosen modulus, which can exceed the ramification support
reason: The theorem defines Q as the places where the tame character ramifies. Lean uses the field ϑ.Q: it only requires the tame part to be trivial outside Q. For a trivial tame part with one permitted auxiliary place in Q, the source’s twist idele is a uniformizer there. Taking actual ramification instead makes it a unit and incorrectly tightens both lattice bounds at that place.
proposed_correction: Let Q be the designated modulus set of the TameChar throughout the statement and induction. Write the bounds with the idele of this Q, and reserve identification with the support of the tame part for twists with the extra nontriviality assumption.

title: Restrict unipotent covariance to degree at least two
reason: The all-stage property gives no qualification on transformation by the unipotent character. The source imposes W(ur)=ψ_U(u)W(r) only when u−1 raises grades by at least two. At stages with positive even string length there can be degree-one directions. The proof establishes no such scalar transformation law for them.
proposed_correction: Define U^{≥2} by the degree condition on u−1 and state the transformation law on this subgroup. It coincides with the whole unipotent radical when the string length is odd.

title: Erasing long rows does not give the stated lift valuation by itself
reason: The remark says the stage lift is divisible to db for the chosen set of erased places. The charged-jet theorem actually bounds the norm by p^(fillingCharge−db), under a condition on the charges for all partners. The neighbor lift also pays the Hecke and low-column costs. The direct p^(−db) bound in ValuationAtNonSplitPrimes.lean:66 is for the empty set and standard data at a non-split prime.
proposed_correction: Describe db as the contribution to the exponent before charges. State the direct estimate for the empty set, and give either the fillingCharge−db jet exponent or the full marked-neighbor exponent when explaining nonempty sets.

title: The edge steps parametrize δKₗ, not Kₗδ
reason: Part 2 calls the cosets right cosets, but δ⁻¹δ′ ∈ Kₗ tests equality of the left cosets δKₗ. At g=1, k=2, r=1 all steps βd give the same right coset Kₗβd=Kₗd; β=1 and an upper unipotent with upper-right entry 1 give distinct left cosets because the latter matrix is outside Pᵣ.
proposed_correction: Put Kₗ=GLₙ(Oₗ), write δ_g(β)Kₗ throughout part 2, and call these left cosets, or cosets modulo right multiplication by Kₗ.

title: The positive root variable at the distinguished letter has an extra unit of weight
reason: For distinct root indices the weight of uᵢ is q/(q−1), while the displayed rule gives 1/(q−1). Thus the purported defect of every monomial containing uᵢ is short by its exponent there. This defect is used in the root lemma and later dimension conditions.
proposed_correction: Add +1 to the indicated weight on uᵢ, in addition to the signed cyclic contribution. Equivalently add the exponent of uᵢ to the weighted degree.

title: Unequal weights do not force vanishing over arbitrary rings
reason: The definition allows arbitrary commutative W and O. Take W=O=𝔽₂, k=2 and distinct block labels. The Levi group is trivial, so extracting the coefficient of X₀₁ is invariant, yet it sends X₀₁ to 1 even for weights ρ=(1,0). The cited vanishing lemma assumes W local and O a characteristic-zero domain with a positive integer nonunit.
proposed_correction: State those extra hypotheses before asserting vanishing, or give the more general sufficient condition of a separating unit whose character difference acts injectively.

title: The nonzero vector belongs to the source of each rectangular matrix
reason: For each nonzero v in kᵐ the theorem bounds both the π-stabilizer mass of A₀v and the inverse-transpose-stabilizer mass of A₁v. Either image can be zero. If A₀=0 then every determinant vanishes, even when the action is transitive on the ambient nonzero vectors and their stabilizers have small mass.
proposed_correction: Quantify over v in kᵐ with v≠0 and state the two stabilizer bounds on its respective images, including a zero image.

title: The common Hecke algebra ranges over spaces with the fixed finite local model
reason: The product is indexed by pointed hermitian spaces having Gram matrix 1 at every finite place and the prescribed diagonal signs at infinity, as defined in Lib/Adelic/Unitary/Defs.lean:498. Rank alone permits other finite local classes. The single common group-algebra element must also preserve principal-level fixed vectors in every representation.
proposed_correction: Specify the common finite adelic model and varying signs, together with a spherical representative preserving principal-level invariants.

title: Define the split Hecke operators for i greater than the rank
reason: The diagonal matrix diag(ϖ1_i,1_(r−i)) belongs to GL_r only for 0 ≤ i ≤ r. The page uses it to define T_(w,i) for every i≥0. The source’s basic double coset is empty for i>r, so T_(w,i)=0 at split off-level places as well. The eigensystem index ranges over all natural numbers.
proposed_correction: Use the displayed double coset for 0 ≤ i ≤ r, and explicitly set T_(w,i)=0 for i>r. State that its restrictions are taken on forms of the pointed spaces with the standard finite model.

title: Correct the indexing family of the spherical Hecke algebra
reason: The page takes the family over all rank-r Hermitian spaces. The product defining the algebra actually ranges over Space E RowIndex s, whose objects include x with x*Jx = 1 at each finite place and diag(s) at each infinite place. A form outside the finite local class has no coordinate of this family, and a point is needed to define the action.
proposed_correction: Define the product over all sign vectors and pointed hermitian spaces having that standard adelic model. Link that definition here so every use of the common algebra inherits the correct domain.

title: The lattice change of basis does not exist over every ring
reason: The description uses x_(k₀)/π̄ + z/N for arbitrary R, although π is a finite idele and N may be zero in R. Over R = 𝔽_N the rational middle form has a radical at z, whereas the lattice middle form has an invertible block with rows (0,−1) and (−1,0) on the distinguished coordinate and z. They cannot be related by a basis change there.
proposed_correction: Define the universal matrix by its distinguished block with rows (0,−1) and (−1,−N) and identity on the other coordinates. Explain the basis change over the finite adeles, or over a ring with a unit π satisfying ππ̄ = N.

title: The finite coefficient ring is a product of completed fields
reason: The page identifies A with a product of localized rings of integers. In the finite application A=∏_{w∈T} E_w. The compact open integer subring is ∏ O_w. A localization of the global integers at w is countable and does not give the completed local field used for Haar integration.
proposed_correction: Define A as the product of the local-field completions over the conjugation-stable finite set T. Identify the product of their rings of integers as its integral subring.

title: The direct-sum kernel needs the product of the two twists
reason: The combined kernel has twists (a, ββ′), while the two factors have (a, β) and (a, β′). The page suppresses the characters without giving this relation. Using the same two twists in all three kernels, for instance, counts β twice on the product side.
proposed_correction: Fix a, β, β′ and specify the three character pairs in the assumed exchange identity, the product formula and its summed version.

title: The remainder tends to zero for odd d coprime to q
reason: The chapter-wide notation only assumes that d is prime and q ≥ 1. The independent prime number theorem in this paragraph also requires d ≠ 2 and gcd(d,q)=1. For d=q=3 every n≡1 mod 3 has (n/3)=1, so the entire weighted sum is zero and R₃(y)=−log(y)/2−c₃ tends to minus infinity.
proposed_correction: State the hypotheses d odd and (d,q)=1 here. Specify likewise at line 49 that the quadratic prime is coprime to the conductor of the primitive character, as holds in the residue class used in the proof.

title: Some imprimitive characters acquire no additional zeros
reason: The remark assigns extra imaginary-axis zeros to imprimitive characters in general. Inducing the nontrivial primitive character modulo 3 to modulus 9 leaves every value on integers unchanged. The two L-functions coincide, as there is no new prime divisor of the modulus.
proposed_correction: Say that imprimitive characters can acquire zeros on Re s = 0 from factors 1−ψ(p)p^(−s) for primes p dividing the modulus and not the conductor.

title: The even-denominator Jacobi symbol needs its convention
reason: Part 1 ranges over every b≥1. The classical Jacobi symbol has odd positive denominator, and the usual Kronecker extension gives (3/2)=−1. The character modulo 2 in Lean necessarily takes value 1 on every odd integer, including 3, so that extension cannot be used in the displayed claim.
proposed_correction: Define the project’s extension by prime factorization, taking the factor at 2 to be 1 on odd numerators and 0 on even ones. Alternatively state the odd-denominator specialization and restrict the induction accordingly.

title: The application cites an integer bound for a real-variable hypothesis
reason: The cited eventually_primeRemainder_natCast_le controls integer x only. The hypothesis at line 17 quantifies over every sufficiently large real x, and New.grh invokes eventually_primeRemainder_le_rpow with ε=β−1/2 after the floor comparison and absorption of constants.
proposed_correction: Link to the real-variable theorem eventually_primeRemainder_le_rpow or to step 2 of the one-sided-bound page. If retaining the explicit constant, label that estimate as the integer intermediate result.

title: The displayed residue function is undefined at zero
reason: The first branch covers every s≠1, including s=0, where s(1−s)=0. The linked polar definition takes a function on all of ℂ, although its residue requirement only concerns Re s>0. Lean assigns 0 at both denominator zeros.
proposed_correction: Use the quotient for s outside {0,1} and set r(0)=r(1)=0, or explicitly restrict the displayed residue law to Re s>0 and extend r arbitrarily elsewhere.

title: The Cauchy citation assumes a holomorphic neighborhood at the boundary
reason: Line 19 assumes complex differentiability at each point of the region, whereas the linked slope lemma asks for F to be holomorphic at every point of the closed disc. For A=0 and R=0, the function F(z)=min(Re z,0)² satisfies line 19 on Re z≥0 and has derivative zero on the boundary, yet it is not holomorphic on any neighborhood of the disc's leftmost point 0. Lean applies the estimate with interior holomorphy and continuity on the closed disc.
proposed_correction: State the slope lemma and its use with F complex differentiable at each point of the closed disc. Apply Cauchy's estimate on the interior and pass to the boundary by continuity, or explicitly take the limit along smaller concentric circles.

title: The product estimate requires an integer cutoff
reason: The proof infers b ≥ a+1 from b > a. As written a need only be nonnegative: with a = 3/2 and S = {2}, the claimed inequality reads 1/2 ≥ 3/5. Also the quotient is 0/0 when a = 0 and S is empty in ordinary arithmetic.
proposed_correction: For the stated application take a to be a positive integer and give the empty-set base case. To include all natural a as in Lean, write (a+|S|) times the product ≥ a, which includes the zero denominator.

title: The splitting interpretation needs d≡3 modulo 4
reason: The support formula in terms of the Legendre symbol holds for all prime d, but the title and the final sentence interpret it as splitting in ℚ(√−d) without repeating the necessary qualification. For d=5, q=1, the prime 3 splits because X²+5 reduces to (X−1)(X+1) modulo 3, yet (3/5)=−1 and λ(3)=2 log 3.
proposed_correction: Keep the formula for general prime d. Explicitly restrict the splitting interpretation to d≡3 mod 4, as the character definition does, and qualify the title or describe the support using χ_K(pᵏ)≠1.

title: The summary gives the derivative bound to the unregularized L-function
reason: The summary says all L-functions have bounded logarithmic derivative on this disc. For a principal character, L′/L = −1/(s−1) + O(1) near 1, so it is unbounded on every punctured disc about 1. The proposition itself correctly bounds Eχ′/Eχ.
proposed_correction: Name the pole-removed functions Eχ in the summary and state the bound for their logarithmic derivatives.

title: Identify the ramified source of the normalized Poincaré maps
reason: The normalized maps in lines 55–59 have domain the ramified subspace, while unqualified source forms elsewhere denote the larger space on X₀. Theorem A spans the ramified space, and the dimension in Theorem B’s cardinality estimate is the dimension of that same subspace.
proposed_correction: Define 𝒮 as the ramified source at the start of this section and retain that meaning in both dimension estimates.

title: Retain the near-full dimension bound when invoking Theorem C
reason: The assembly paragraph records only n ≥ d_T/2 before applying Theorem C. The theorem as stated at line 60 needs n ≥ (1−4/b²)d_T, which is strictly stronger here. Lean constructs the family with that bound, uses it at line 134, and only then weakens it to d_T/2 for division.
proposed_correction: Give n ≥ (1−4/b²)d_T when choosing the family. Use n ≤ d_T and nonnegativity of h_main+F for cancellation and reserve the half-dimension estimate for dividing the error by n.

title: A complex Gram determinant need not be a squared lattice covolume
reason: The definition accepts any finite family. In ℂ the vectors 1 and i have Hermitian Gram determinant zero, yet generate ℤ[i] of real covolume one. Even for complex-independent (1,0),(i,1) in ℂ² the Hermitian determinant is 1 and the squared real covolume of their ℤ-span in its real span is 2.
proposed_correction: Describe the determinant as the squared Hermitian exterior norm of the family. To identify it with a real lattice covolume, specify an appropriate real structure and lattice hypotheses.

title: The different bound and the size of b give separate inequalities
reason: Membership of q₁d in the different shows rd_E≤q₁d. It does not show q₁d≤b, the final inequality in the displayed chain. Lean uses the large-scale estimates for the latter comparison before selecting the level prime.
proposed_correction: Use rd_E≤q₁d from the norm of the different, then q₁d≤Wⁿ≤exp(W⁶)≤b from the large-scale bounds.

title: The last estimate in the scale row needs the tower bound
reason: The first four estimates exponentiate (S2)–(S5). The fifth, x₁^(3l₀²)≤√b, also needs l₀≤81s and the upper bound on s. The proof’s assertion about the entire row conceals a dependence on the tower exponent.
proposed_correction: State l₀≤81s and s≤32 log x≤log x₁. Then 3l₀² log x₁≤3·81²(log x₁)³≤(log x₁)⁶/2≤(log b)/2 since log x₁ is large.

title: The Weil-height comparison fails already for a rational constant
reason: For y_ι=2, take H=1/2, α=−log 2 and h_ℓ=0 for every ℓ. Then Hy_ι=1 and the definition holds with c=−log 2, while the logarithmic Weil height of 2 is log 2 even before any degree normalization. The appeal to a one-sided Weil-height bound can therefore mislead readers about what c bounds.
proposed_correction: Replace the comparison by the rational example. More generally for rational z≠0 the least possible c is −log|z|, realized by H=1/z and bounded below by the height product formula with c′=log|z|.

title: Identify the restricted map in the single-lift determinant
reason: The page describes Z_j as the determinant of the j-th single lift. The single lift acts on all principal-level forms on W_j. Lean forms the endomorphism u* u after restricting the lift to the good forms on W_j. The determinant on the full source is a different expression, and the equality of source dimension to d_T is stated for the good forms.
proposed_correction: Define Z_j(ϑʲ) = det(u* u), where u is the single lift for the character ϑʲ restricted to the good forms on W_j. The same restriction applies at the trivial twist.

title: Give the hypotheses on powers and reciprocal bounds
reason: Lean multiplies an exponent by A in the stated order for natural A. For F=2 with lower exponent 0, taking A=−1 would incorrectly give 1≤1/2. Also the upper bound |F|≤eˡ gives a lower exponent −l for F⁻¹ only for positive F, as the separate instance at line 304 requires.
proposed_correction: State A∈ℕ for the power rule. For the reciprocal, a lower exponent gives the upper exponent, and an upper exponent plus F>0 gives the lower exponent.

title: Specify which false lifts enter the projection bound
reason: Orthogonality to false lifts depends on an idempotent and a subspace. Lean uses the good-forms idempotent e₀ and the orthogonal complement of Zϑ,j. The linked general predicate also allows a different subspace, such as the kernel of descent for a test form.
proposed_correction: Require y to be orthogonal to the false lifts for (e₀, Zϑ,j⊥) at every split place off the level, with the good-forms idempotent e₀.

title: State the zero-denominator convention in the Behrend bound
reason: Parts 1 and 2 allow n=0 or H=0 but give the ordinary quotient Hⁿ/(nH²). Lean’s real division gives zero in these cases, while that quotient is undefined in the prose. For n=H=1 there is exactly one squared radius, so the proof’s strict count of fewer than nH² radii also fails.
proposed_correction: For n,H≥1 use “at most nH² radii”. Cover nH=0 separately with lower bound zero and the empty set, or explicitly restrict the first two parts to positive n,H and note the degenerate cases.

title: Specify the level and weight of the lifted forms
reason: The construction calls the level trivial at the chosen places and block upper triangular at Q. These are conditions on reductions of integral matrices. The local level at a chosen place is a principal congruence subgroup. Describing only the weight and character ‘attached to ϑ’ also leaves the space S_ϑ unidentified in the defining paragraph.
proposed_correction: Specify integral elements reducing to the identity at the chosen places and to the indicated parabolic at Q. Identify the fixed Weyl weight from columnsY and lastEntry(m) and cite the level character, which applies the tame characters to determinants of the diagonal blocks.

title: Verify the full source is nonzero before applying the few-maps theorem
reason: The cited theorem requires both spaces to be nonzero. The page proves positive target dimension and bounds ε₀, but gives no reason D_X>0. If the full source were zero and the target positive dimensional, every map would satisfy the stated spread condition while their images would span zero.
proposed_correction: Add that the source coordinate isomorphism identifies the full source with the nonzero space of complex vectors indexed by the pairs of a class and a Bessel coordinate. This is the nontriviality established in ShortAndEnough immediately before the theorem is applied.

title: The determinant norm has a lower bound and the cost is additive in valuations
reason: The argument bounds the weighted sum of the determinant valuations above by v(π) times the sum of the deductions. Equivalently the product of the determinant norms, each with its column multiplicity κ(τ,h), is bounded below by |π| raised to that sum. Bounding this product above by the sum itself can already give 1 ≤ 0 when no congruences are imposed. Pairing divisibility is required only for nonexempt pairs.
proposed_correction: State the bound on the weighted sum of valuations and restrict the pairing conclusion to nonexempt pairs.

title: The Frobenius description of the decomposition group is unramified
reason: The pair (χ_K(p)p,χ_K(p)) generates the decomposition group in the cited result when p does not divide q₁d. At p=d its second component is zero and does not represent either Galois sign. This matters in a chapter that also treats p=d.
proposed_correction: Specify p ∤ q₁d before using the Frobenius element for the decomposition group, and distinguish the separate residue congruence at the ramified prime.

title: Justify why every root of unity here is a power of ζ
reason: Kronecker’s theorem gives finite order for an integral norm-one γ. The next inference γ=ζᵏ uses a special property of E. Merely adjoining a primitive q₁-th root to a CM field does not ensure that it generates all roots of unity. This fact is needed to make the tame factor trivial.
proposed_correction: Name Kronecker’s theorem and link parts 6 and 7 of proofs/grh/reduction-main/field-e-properties, which prove μ(E)=⟨ζ⟩, N(E/K)(ζ)=1 and the product formula for the chosen embeddings.

title: The deduction is an attainable cost, not a minimum
reason: The source constructs one covering choice of this cost. With N=3, no marks, one height-two column on each side, p=3 and e=1, the displayed D is 1. Imposing only the source-entry conditions at every height covers every pair and costs 2/3 by the source’s definitions of cost and covering.
proposed_correction: Describe D as the cost of the specified covering choice and an upper bound on the required determinant loss. Remove the global optimality claim.

title: The integrality input concerns twisted torsion values
reason: For a degree-n section f the library controls the image of f[u]=f(u) exp(−nπ|u|²/(2 area Λ)). Its isogeny pullback preserves these normalized values with the degree multiplied by q. Plain values f(u), as the text calls them, have an extra factor whose p-adic norm the cited result does not control.

title: The third matrix shape has up to twice the stated number of entries
reason: The proof says each of the three exponents is at most n_m² before saying the third may use two such bounds. Its actual exponent is (n_{2i}+n_{2i+2})n_{2i+1}, for which the source uses 2n_m². For the last pair this exponent is 2n_{m−1}² by the rank progression.
proposed_correction: Write the three bounds as n_m², n_m² and 2n_m². Their sum is at most 4n_m², which gives divisibility by 𝒞⁴.

title: The odd glued Gram matrix leaves mixed entries unspecified
reason: The list specifies the pairing of y with the middle z_c and all pairings within the string, but leaves the values of ⟨y,z_b⟩ and ⟨z_b,y⟩ for b≠c open when s is odd. These entries are zero in the mixed block of gluedGram.
proposed_correction: Set both mixed pairings to zero for each b≠c, or end the list by setting all unspecified matrix entries to zero.

title: Odd string length alone does not prevent self-duality
reason: The standard Gram matrix for s=1 and N=1 is diag(I,−1), which is already unimodular. For odd s the obstruction over the integral lattice is that N is a nonunit, since every other block is already unimodular.
proposed_correction: State that the unglued standard lattice fails to be self-dual at places where N is a nonunit. Specify that this occurs at the places over the level prime in the application.

title: Define the scalar for an arbitrary archimedean function
reason: The theorem allows every function a without a measurability or integrability hypothesis. The displayed ordinary integral of aα can therefore be undefined, even for a zero integrand f in the theorem. Lean takes the totalized Bochner integral of a against the measure with density α, including the nonintegrable case.
proposed_correction: Define κ using the weighted integral of a when a is integrable for that measure, and set κ=0 otherwise. State the totalized product-integral convention used in the factorization, or give its integrable and nonintegrable cases explicitly.

title: Supply a graded point in the Bessel orbit
reason: The support theorem bounds every translate whose lattice is graded. To conclude that the orbit is bounded one needs a translate with graded lattice. The source uses the existence theorem for graded translates, invoking the primitive 5040th root of unity in the field of the data.
proposed_correction: Invoke part 3 of lattice-bounds-induction-step to obtain a graded representative, then apply the support bound to that representative before using the cut multiplicity theorem.

title: Lengths 1, 0, 0 do not by themselves define the last double lift
reason: HasConsecutiveStrings also requires that the generic constants of Y and Y′ agree. The last case only lists the lengths, and genericConst is a freely specified nonzero conjugation-invariant element in each grading. The last-double-lift construction requires this compatibility even though the subsequent coordinate calculation only uses the lengths.
proposed_correction: Add c_Y=c_Y′ as a common hypothesis of both cases and link the definition of consecutive strings. In particular make it explicit in the last case.

title: Use Petersson nondegeneracy to separate the forms
reason: The text calls the space of all test forms on Y_m finite-dimensional. FormY fixes the archimedean type and allows varying finite level. The available finite-dimensionality theorem requires a fixed level. Lean uses nondegeneracy of the inner product for the whole form space.
proposed_correction: Let v be the difference of the two forms, set x=v in the equality of pairings, and conclude from ⟨v,v⟩=0.

title: Qualify the identification with the zero-term lattice
reason: The remark identifies the constructed lattice with the zero-term lattice of a pair of edges without specifying hypotheses on the pair. The source requires a split prime, a middle grading spanning the prescribed lattice, and an integral lift for each neighbour vector. These hypotheses enter the proof of lattice containment.
proposed_correction: State the identification for pairs satisfying the spanning and neighbour-lifting conditions at the split level. Link to part 1 of the admissible-evaluation-of-edge-pairs knowl, which states the identification.

title: Distinguish the explicit sum from a sum over all lattice classes
reason: The summary describes a full system of representatives. The admissibility of the displayed sum needs only split squarefreeness, as its statement says. The separate theorem that these vectors exhaust the lattice classes also requires a split level, in particular residue degree one at the selected places. A split squarefree factorization alone does not identify each residue field with ℤ/N.
proposed_correction: State the admissibility result for the explicitly indexed sum as written, and qualify its interpretation as the sum over all neighbour-lattice classes by the split-level hypothesis.

title: The denominator is a natural cardinal that can be zero
reason: Both the definition and theorem use the usual cardinality |Ô/(β)| to define an integer denominator, and line 117 divides it by K as an integer. Lean takes the natural cardinal of the entire matrix set, zero if infinite. For example, take δ=κ=1, X′ nonempty and β equal to 1 everywhere except β_v=0 for one v away from N. The scaling hypotheses hold while Ô/(β) has the infinite quotient Ô_v.
proposed_correction: Define D_β as the size of (Ô/(β))^{I×X′} if finite and zero otherwise. Its divisibility by K then includes the infinite case. Alternatively add a finite-quotient hypothesis and identify that version as the specialization used for the tower.

title: The chosen modulus is more general than the exact ramification set
reason: For TameChar the tame factors must be trivial outside Q and may also be trivial at places in Q. The point-mass operator nevertheless uses every place of Q in its modulus. Replacing Q by the actual ramification set can change Φ_k and its level even for the same underlying character.
proposed_correction: Call Q the chosen modulus supporting the tame part, including in the summary's description of q. Retain the stated product of norms and the condition Q=∅.

title: Use the prescribed modulus set of a tame character
reason: The set Q of a TameChar is allowed to include places with trivial tame part. A trivial character with a permitted nonempty Q still has a twist idele of uniformizer valuation at those extra places, so using its actual ramification set would give the wrong idele and point-datum modulus.
proposed_correction: Introduce Q as the chosen conjugate-disjoint finite modulus set containing the support of the tame part. The stronger condition that every place of Q has nontrivial tame part is imposed for a Twist.

title: The projection averages over the conjugate places as well
reason: For S the primes dividing 𝔪, projOn S averages integral translations supported on S∪conj(S). The description only mentions places dividing 𝔪. By contrast the input residue function is read only on S: the lift is zero when the S-part is nonintegral and ignores coordinates off S.
proposed_correction: Define P^𝔪 as the normalized mean over translations on S∪conj(S). Specify that the lifted function takes x to Ψ(red(1_S x)) when 1_S x is integral and to zero otherwise.

title: State the terminal identity in joint invariance
reason: The description of what it means to be a chain datum says the levels of the U(X_j) fix its tensor, after listing X_0 through X_m. The defined action requires b_m=1 and permits the level factors to vary for j<m. Allowing the terminal level to act freely is a stronger condition than the one used in the existence proof.
proposed_correction: Specify that the tensor is fixed by tuples with b_j in the level for j<m and b_m=1. Link this bullet to property 1 of the seesaw datum.

title: The cuts use a chosen modulus that can exceed the ramification set
reason: Q is allowed to contain places where the tame character is trivial. J_j imposes its congruences at all places of this supplied Q. Computing J_j from the exact ramification set instead can change the quotient and the cuts.
proposed_correction: Describe Q as the finite modulus supporting the tame part, and take q to be the product of the norms of all its places.

title: The initial cut needs invariance of the chosen level
reason: Ω₀ consists of classes of the chosen level, whereas the chosen stage cuts for j>0 are invariant under the integral Bessel subgroup. Knowing that the image of level X₀ lies in K₀ does not imply it preserves those chosen-level classes, and Ω₀ was not defined as a stage cut.
proposed_correction: For j=0 use xJ₀∈Ω₀ iff x belongs to the chosen level and the fact that the image of level X₀ is contained in that chosen level. Its multiplicity is identically one. Apply the stage-cut argument for j>0.

title: Define the adelic coefficient of the upper algebraic form
reason: The core writes t(ψ(diag(k,1))) for an adelic k. The algebraic form ψ is a vector-valued function on finite points. Its coefficient at h=diag(k,1) also uses the action of h_∞⁻¹ on that vector. The phrase about coefficients in line 42 leaves this operation implicit in the lemma whose integral uses it.
proposed_correction: Set h=diag(k,1) and write F(k)=t(ρ(h_∞⁻¹)ψ(h_f)), identifying ρ with the conjugate Weyl representation. This also fixes the meaning of the coefficient reused by the lower-chain proof.

title: Identify the target of the evaluated datum, including the last pair
reason: The display introduces X″_{2i+2} without identifying it with the tower index X_{2i+2}. The last grading has definite part InitIndex(m), of size n_m−1, and the last double lift adjoins precisely the line that restores X_m. Leaving this unresolved obscures why this datum is an input to the next definite lift or to the terminal coefficient.
proposed_correction: Use Hom(X_{2i+1},X_{2i+2}) in the second factor. In the final grading identify the definite part as InitIndex(m), write X_m=InitIndex(m) ⊔ {∗}, and note that the final grading has constant 1.

title: Use odd string length in the uniqueness step
reason: Equivariance alone gives transformation only for the subgroup where u−1 has degree at least two. Agreement on U(X_{2i+2}) determines the function here because m−1−(2i+2) is odd, so every unipotent at the induction stage belongs to that subgroup. The source supplies this parity when applying uniqueness.
proposed_correction: State that the terminal string of this induction step is odd and invoke the odd-length uniqueness lemma before concluding equality on the full Bessel group.

title: Quotient by the rational points over the fixed field
reason: The display uses R_{k+1}(E) for the divisor in the quotient, with E the CM field. The rational unitary subgroup is defined over its totally real fixed field F and consists of the E-rational matrices satisfying unitarity, inside the adelic group. After base change to E, the algebraic group’s E-points are a different group. Lean takes the intersection of the rational unitary group with the adelic Bessel subgroup.
proposed_correction: Write R_{k+1}(F)\G_{k+1}, F=E⁺, or define Γ_{R_{k+1}}=Γ_{Y_{k+1}}∩R_{k+1} and use that subgroup in both places in the formula.

title: Only a selected sparse subset of class −1 receives weight b
reason: The parallel descriptions of the a- and b-places suggest that both are entire residue classes. All class-1 places are a-places, whereas the b-places are selected inside class −1 and satisfy a sparseness condition. Other class-−1 places receive a/x₁. This distinction changes the total F(p) used without definition at line 27.
proposed_correction: Name Φ_b as the chosen sparse subset of class −1 and define F(p)=∑σ sₚ(w(σ),σ) when displaying the gain.

title: Full marks cover the conjugate pairs arising from a-places
reason: The quantified requirement is that for each a-place τ, either its induced prime or its conjugate lies in Λ. The phrase “every conjugate pair” extends this to unrelated primes above p. Marked sets in this argument also have p<x₁.
proposed_correction: State that for each a-place its induced prime or its conjugate is marked, at a small exceptional nonsplit prime.

title: The quoted chain identity has a different source
reason: The proof and its status paragraph attribute the three principal inputs to CharactersAtLevel.lean. The gluing-to-direct-chain induction is in LiftLawsModuloN.lean, while the local Weil-action and double-gluing formulas are in Columns.lean. The norm-comparison citation in step 1 also omits the IsSplitLevel namespace.
proposed_correction: Cite LiftLawsModuloN.lean:895 for step 5, Columns.lean:292 and :522 for steps 2 and 4, and New.IsSplitLevel.norm_detCharAt_diagN_anti at Columns.lean:341 for step 1.

title: Assign denominators only to the nonzero losses
reason: The proof says every term in every finite U can be assigned to one of four slots per c≤x₁. An arbitrarily large U can have more than 4⌊x₁⌋ elements. The source bounds every unserved value by zero instead. With U allowed to contain zero, the ordinary-real expression 0·log 0 also needs a convention.
proposed_correction: Define the weighted term to be zero whenever the allowed loss vanishes and discard those terms, including p=0, before assigning the remaining primes and N to slots.

title: The class sum is taken after the integrands are combined
reason: The proof starts by treating each single lift as a sum over the stated level classes. For a fixed x the integrand can vary on a K_j-coset. Joint invariance proves right K_j-invariance of the sum over x, with the last kernel included, before its integral is evaluated as a class sum (lines 253–267).
proposed_correction: Start with the class integral. Sum the integrands over x, apply joint invariance to that sum, and then use trivial stabilizers to replace its integral by the unweighted sum.

title: The advertised projection lemma is missing
reason: The declaration list includes projOn_translateDatum. The page ends its four claims without stating that projection onto the vacuum at S fixes a translated datum whenever its translation is integral on S and its conjugate. The Hecke-transfer proof invokes exactly this property (ValuationAtNonSplitPrimes.lean, lines 402–412).
proposed_correction: Add the implication that integrality of x_j at S ∪ conjugate(S) gives projOn(S) Φ⁰_{x,j} = Φ⁰_{x,j}, and identify the integral translations in the projector that fix the local vacuum.

title: The local insertion depends on the vacuum projection of the input
reason: For general v, “replace its component” does not define the linear operator in the theorem. The Schrödinger operator is a sum of Heisenberg translates of the local vacuum projection of v. In particular its value is zero if that projection vanishes, a case that occurs in the translated-vacuum argument on this page.
proposed_correction: Define Dirⱼ(v) by applying the local Schrödinger operator of the direct datum to v and then applying the Weil action of (δⱼ,δⱼ₊₁). Explain that the local operator factors through the projection onto the vacuum.

title: The two estimates used to prove the gauge bound have incorrect qualified names
reason: The Fourier expansion is New.Seesaw.isAdmissibleCombination_schrodingerOp_of_reduction, and the standard-data bound is New.Parameters.mem_raises_of_standardData in UpperBound/Kernels/ThetaLiftGauge.lean:298. The direct-datum definition in line 15 also belongs to New.IsSplitLevel. All three have matching translated pages.
proposed_correction: Link the existing schrodinger-operator-admissible, gauge-bounds-for-one-lift and data-modulo-n knowls, or use their correct qualified names.

title: Specify the inverse transpose in the origin’s quotient coordinate
reason: In the stated quotient GLₖ(W)/Pᵣ, the origin coordinate is gₑ⁻ᵀPᵣ. The criterion gₑᵀ(gₑ′ᵀ)⁻¹ ∈ Pᵣ compares those cosets or equivalently the opposite cosets Pᵣgₑᵀ. It does not compare gₑᵀPᵣ and gₑ′ᵀPᵣ, as the unqualified “coset of gₑᵀ” can suggest in this quotient.
proposed_correction: Write the coordinate as (o(e), gₑ⁻ᵀPᵣ), or explicitly say that Pᵣgₑᵀ is a coset on the opposite side.

title: The divisibility interpretation omits the restricted source module
reason: The cited theorem guarantees gain minus error on a submodule of controlled colength in the integral ramified source forms. Its quantified valuation conclusion at lines 508–509 assumes membership in that submodule. The remark describes it as a conclusion about an integral source form without this condition.
proposed_correction: Say that the divisibility holds for forms in the submodule supplied for the chosen prime and embedding, and for twists of modulus prime to p.

title: The archimedean norm in the bound is unspecified
reason: The bare squared norm in part 3 is specifically the Weyl Gram norm Re(ξ*Gξ), with the Gram matrix for the corresponding module on each side. The branching estimate invoked in the proof controls that norm. An ordinary coordinate norm does not inherit the stated constant from it.
proposed_correction: Specify the Weyl Gram norms in part 3 and link the branching-map knowl. Its defining properties are New.Data.IsBranchingMap.mul_weylRep and New.Data.IsBranchingMap.weylNormSq_le in Objects/Columns.lean, lines 681 and 690.

title: Right translation is summed over left cosets
reason: The proof asks for representatives of right cosets. Its action on a Kₗ-fixed form factors through δKₗ because changing δ to δk fixes the summand. Choosing representatives modulo multiplication on the left does not have this invariance.
proposed_correction: Write the sum over the left cosets δKₗ in KₗdKₗ and retain the right translation of the form by each representative.

title: Identify the character whose value enters the transfer polynomial
reason: Part 1 names a rank-twisted base change, and part 3 calls χ the unit value of “the lift character.” Lean takes χ from the unrank-twisted base change of ν_{e+1} at the uniformizer. The two rank-twisted base changes supply the unramifiedness hypotheses, while their space characters both reduce to ν_{e+1}’s base change by evenness of the ranks (lines 495–515). Confusing these values changes the factors of R.
proposed_correction: Define χ = ν_{e+1}^{BC}(ϖ_l). Explain the even-rank space-character cancellation giving the Frobenius values z^{n_e}χ and z^{n_{e+1}}χ. In the quoted pairing theorem use its actual name New.SiegelWeil.hecke_transfer_of_pairing.

title: The global regrouping fails for arbitrary derivative order
reason: The local definition allows any real y. The global prime sum stops at ν=a, whereas the local sums include all prime powers. Choose e with d^e>a and then y>d^e max(w). The ramified prime-power term is positive in the local sum and omitted from the global sum. All terms are nonnegative.
proposed_correction: Qualify the identity with y≤a, as in primeSum_eq_sum_localPrimeSum. Under this hypothesis all terms with p^e≥x₁ vanish and one may sum over primes below any integer U≥ceil(x₁).

title: The jet criterion ranges over the whole standard-data module
reason: The text says it suffices to check every vacuum translate in the given datum. The criterion quantifies over every standard f. In its proof the original datum is moved by integral group elements before testing its jets (lines 215–228), so checking only its original summands is insufficient. The charged-jet theorem actually provides the requisite uniformity.
proposed_correction: Quantify over all standard f, or use all standard vacuum-translate generators and extend by integral linearity and the ultrametric inequality. Specify the kernel's jet scale and use the New.Parameters namespace for omega_mem_raises_of_schurJet_le, norm_schurJet_jetSeries_le_of_charges and mem_raises_predictedDivisibility.

title: The jet size does not have global linear growth
reason: The summary says the jet size grows at most linearly. For fixed data s∞(l)=log(l!)+l log(M/Ω), so s∞(l)/l is unbounded. Part 2 in the body correctly retains log(r′+e+1) in the increment per added box.
proposed_correction: Describe the estimate as an upper bound on the cost of e added boxes, at most e[log(r′+e+1)+log(M/Ω)]. A linear bound with a fixed slope requires a specified bound on row length.

title: The cokernel estimate requires reduction modulo p^j
reason: The remark attributes a controlled length to the full cokernel on the integral module M. The cited theorem bounds the colength of T̃M + p^j M in M for each j, with a bound that grows with j. This permits a free part in the full cokernel and does not supply a finite length bound for it.
proposed_correction: Say that the scaling preserves M and bounds the colength of T̃M + p^j M in M at every specified j.

title: The short test vectors use conjugate weight embeddings
reason: The displayed A is described as using the embeddings of the CM type. Lean forms both its determinant factors and its Weyl matrix with weightEmbedding, x ↦ Φ_τ(conj x) over ℂ and x ↦ ι(Φ_τ(conj x)) over ℂ_p (ShortColumns.lean:386–389). Replacing this by Φ_τ(x) can read the other prime above p, so the claimed integral matrix after multiplying by c⁻¹ need not follow.
proposed_correction: Define the embedding used for each τ as Φ_τ composed with complex conjugation on E, and use its adelic extension in the integral determinant and Schur calculation.

title: The auxiliary translate must be supported on the marked pairs
reason: Condition (c) specifies g only at primes of Λ and leaves its other components unrestricted. Lean quantifies over a tuple of matrices at Λ and applies its unitary embedding, which is identity outside Λ and its conjugate. The cited base case for one neighbor has exactly this support hypothesis. With Λ empty the printed condition would allow every adelic g while the source tests only 1.
proposed_correction: Define g in (c) as the unitary adelic extension of a tuple at Λ, or require it to be identity outside Λ ∪ conjugate(Λ). The induction then changes just the component at the newly added prime and its conjugate.

title: Identify the normalization of the jets in the integrality argument
reason: The proof describes the jets as scaled by the conjugate of π̄_M. The cited estimate takes a kernel at c·jetScale, and c alone occurs in its norm ratio. The actual lift kernel in Columns.lean:859 uses this full product. Applying the displayed ratio to jets with only the stated scale omits the period normalization used for integrality.
proposed_correction: Write that the already period-normalized jets are multiplied by c=conj(π̄_M), or display the full kernel scale c·jetScale. Keep c alone in the numerator of the estimate.

title: Nakayama uses reductions after division by w^(c−1)
reason: The dimension estimate applies to residues of every h with w^(c−1)h∈C. The chapter records only the smaller set of residues of C before invoking Nakayama. In a valuation ring, C=wO has zero reduction, although all h satisfy wh∈C. A bound only on the former residues cannot justify the generator count.
proposed_correction: Introduce the residue subspace S containing the reductions of all h with w^(c−1)h∈C, give its dimension bound and use that stronger property in the generator argument.

title: The numerical large-degree conditions alone are insufficient for the stated theorem
reason: The chapter states the intertwining assumption separately and links the full theorem. Its displayed colength claim refers only to large degree, although Lean also takes a characteristic-zero valuation domain O with p a nonunit. The opening paragraph allows an arbitrary coefficient ring.
proposed_correction: Name the valuation-domain and nonunit hypotheses beside the displayed result and refer back to the finite edge data and intertwining identity.

title: The comparison with evaluation concerns every conjugate
reason: The summary predicates agreement on the support of ψ alone. A Levi element can exchange a good diagonal variable with a bad one, so a polynomial supported on good monomials need not satisfy the comparison. The core correctly imposes a degree bound and tests every Levi conjugate.
proposed_correction: Describe the summary’s comparison as agreement in degrees ≤D when every Levi conjugate has no bad monomial modulo the chosen ideal.

title: Shallow variables need order one in the zero count
reason: The displayed cases define κ solely from the row index. The conclusion sums only over deep variables, but line 26 uses κ on every variable. For r=1 and k=2 the displayed definition makes the product P^(2N)=q², while the family contains only q points.
proposed_correction: Specify κ(v)=1 for shallow variables and apply the displayed P and P^(2r) branches only to deep variables. This gives the product in the unipotent-points construction and leaves the concluding sum over deep variables intact.

title: An arbitrary depth scaling need not be a twisted group element
reason: The displayed tensor identity holds for every t∈R. The following sentence describes it as evaluation of the twisted GLₖ(W) representation at a diagonal matrix. For t=0, k=2, r=1 and n=1 the depth diagonal has zero entries, while every matrix in the image of a group representation is invertible.
proposed_correction: Describe the operator as the tensor product of symmetric powers of the separate letterwise diagonal matrices given in the display. The displayed identity is sufficient for general t.

title: Ordinary Lebesgue measure is undefined for some allowed sets
reason: The text quantifies over every Y but links to ordinary Lebesgue measure on measurable sets. For k=1, m=0, v=+, P=2, D=1, take a nonmeasurable subset Y of (0,1). The step map is the identity, and both advertised measures are undefined in that convention. Lean’s measure on arbitrary sets is its associated outer measure.
proposed_correction: Use Lebesgue outer measure for arbitrary sets, or state the ordinary-measure version for measurable Y. The downstream cone and slab are measurable.

title: The normalized basis uses an inverse that may not exist
reason: A Frobenius cycle permits a coefficient field of characteristic p with w=0. For a positive-depth monomial the displayed w^(−depth) is then undefined, although the diagonal w^depth is still defined. For instance W=O=𝔽₂₅, p=5, N=2, with the identity and fifth-power maps, admits this cycle.
proposed_correction: Give the diagonal formula for every cycle. Describe the normalized monomial basis in the geometric setting of a domain with w nonzero, inside its fraction field.

title: A single polynomial’s good support does not imply evaluation agreement
reason: Take W=O=ℤ localized at 3, p=3, f=D=1, k=2, a single Levi block, ρ=(1,0) and t=0. The monomial X₁₁ has no bad term, but a permutation conjugates it to the bad X₀₀. Any invariant average kills X₁₁, while scaled evaluation there is 3⁴. The precise guarantee also ends at D, which can be smaller than p^f−1.
proposed_correction: Say that for degree at most D the average agrees modulo J with scaled evaluation if every Levi conjugate has its bad coefficients in J.

title: Saturation can include vectors that vary over one origin
reason: For w=0 the defining condition holds for every ψ with m=1 and φ=0. Take degree n=0 and two edges with the same origin and the same frame. The restriction has equal values on the two edges, while (0,1) belongs to the displayed module. Cycles over a field of characteristic p allow w=0.
proposed_correction: Call the general module the w-power saturation of the restriction image. Explain the interpretation as a restriction after inverting w in the geometric case where w is a non-zero-divisor.

title: Power substitution commutes with the action, while the packing has extra moving factors
reason: The summary attributes equivariance to packing. With k=2, m=q⁰=1 and n=0, packing the single constant 1 gives ∏ₛx_(a,s)². Swapping the two rows fixes the constant and changes this monomial. The correct formula in the body also translates the class monomial x^(γᵤ).
proposed_correction: Say the substitution x↦xᵐ commutes with the action when m=qʲ. Describe the packed translate as a sum in which both the input form and the class monomial are translated.

title: The matrix blocks are the conjugates of the normalized amplitude sums
reason: With the convention declared at line 15, the sum is the pairing ⟨sPe_y,Pe_x⟩. The row-x, column-y entry of P* s P is the conjugate. Squared norms in the next estimate hide this distinction, but the two complex matrices need not agree.
proposed_correction: Insert “complex conjugates of” before “the amplitude sums”, or write the actual Petersson-pairing identity.

title: Include M > 0 in the quoted estimate for good tuples
reason: The stated general estimate omits the assumption NeZero M. If M = 0 then every field element satisfies x^M = 1, so the argument that discards at most M possible roots does not apply. The specialized application uses the positive integer q₂.
proposed_correction: State M ≥ 1 in the auxiliary estimate and mention that q₂ = (q₀d)^(s+6) is positive.

title: Restore the positive-part operation before squaring
reason: For unrestricted real b, Lean squares the nonnegative part of (b⁻¹)^(r³f). With b = −1 and r and f odd, its error coefficient is 0, while the displayed b^(−2r³f) is 1. The scaled length also uses totalized division when b = 0.
proposed_correction: Give the coefficient as max(0,(b⁻¹)^(r³f))² with 0⁻¹ = 0, or explicitly specialize the page to b > 0 and identify the larger domain of IsCutPair.

title: Identify the equality actually supplied by the Bessel degree field
reason: The outline attributes equality with the noncompact formal degree to deg_eq. That field states B.deg = weylDimensionPoly(l). SpanningTheorem.lean lines 99–101 use Harish-Chandra’s identity on the compact formal-degree side and identify the same polynomial on both sides.
proposed_correction: Start from B.deg = weylDimensionPoly(l) and apply the formal-degree formula to the all-positive parameter, whose entries give the same Weyl polynomial.

title: Clarify which operators preserve the subspace
reason: The proof calls the subspace “invariant” in addition to being stable under the T operators, then says the hypotheses hold for principal-level forms. The library requires only simultaneous sphericity and Hecke stability. Invariance of a fixed-level space under the entire adelic representation is generally unavailable as translation changes its level.
proposed_correction: Describe a finite-dimensional subspace that is spherical at the stated places and stable under all their T operators. In the application use the pointed V underlying the principal-level forms.

title: Require the common finite adelic model in the multiplicity theorem
reason: Rank, archimedean signs and the gaps in the theorem body do not impose the finite local condition on V and V′. Each Lean Space carries an adelic point x with x*Jx = 1 at every finite place. A Hermitian form whose determinant has a different local norm class cannot supply such an x, and the fixed finite group and principal level in this comparison have not been identified for it.
proposed_correction: State that both spaces come with adelic bases giving the identity form at each finite place and their respective sign matrices at each infinite place. Link the pointed-space definition before comparing multiplicities.

title: State the finite-place hypothesis of trace comparison
reason: The summary says the spaces differ only at the real places, but the theorem body specifies only rank and archimedean signs. The cited comparison theorem takes two pointed spaces whose finite adelic forms are both identified with the identity. That assumption makes the same J_M, test function and Hecke operator available on the two sides.
proposed_correction: Require the pointed spaces of the project with x*Jx equal to 1 at every finite place and diag(s) or diag(s′) at every infinite place. Carry the condition into the quoted trace-comparison statement in Step 2.

title: Invertibility of Z and W does not guarantee an inverse square root
